images.alt: Tile with text that says: chickenpox vs measles. Know the difference.

Tile with text that says: Chickenpox: Mild to moderate fever 38-39 degrees celcius. Occasional mild headache. Cough, runny nose, sore throat or conjunctivitis is rare. Mild fatigue is common. Mild loss of appetite. Itchy, fluid-filled blisters appear on torso and then spread.

Tile with text that says: Measles: Headache is common. Cough, runny nose and conjunctivitis are common. Fatigue can be moderate to severe. Rash - flat red spots. Starts at hairline and spreads downward. High fever often over 30.5 degrees celcius. Often significant loss of appetite.

post.text:
Is it measles or chickenpox? With measles spreading in NZ, it’s important to know the difference. 

Sometimes, measles is mixed up with chickenpox, but they are two very different illnesses, with measles being more severe.
Both illnesses have vaccines. Check you’re up-to-date.
